name: Sertac Karaman
title: Professor; Director, Autonomy & Embedded Robotics Accelerated (AERA) and Low-Energy Autonomy and Navigation (LEAN)
fitReason: Strong direct intersection of reinforcement learning, learned feasibility models and actual agile aerial robot deployment, with ongoing uncertainty-aware generative modeling research.

physicalEvidence.summary: Multi-fidelity RL replanning uses analytical checks, simulation and actual quadrotor flights to train a reward estimator and sequence-to-sequence policy. The August 7, 2025 full-paper revision documents 50 real-flight test waypoint sequences, motion-capture tracking and mid-flight waypoint changes in a 9 × 9 × 3 m space; the physical-flight table reports peak speed 11 m/s. This is actual learned planning, with an existing low-level controller. The journal article appeared online August 22, 2025 and in the April 2026 issue; the issue date is not evidence of newly conducted 2026 flights. Current availability of that exact testbed is unverified.

shortVisit.summary: Current official faculty and AERA team/research pages were reviewed; no current invitation specifically for external master’s short visits or summer 2027 was located. General MIT visiting-student policy is a conditional institutional process, not a faculty opening.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct RL and Bayesian learned-feasibility methods affect physical flight trajectories.
scoreReasons.physical: Rigorous real quadrotor execution from the 2024/2025 study; conservative 20 because current 2026 rig availability and new physical execution are not independently established.

scoreReasons.freshness: Current official affiliation, April 2026 journal issue, February 2026 uncertainty-aware flow paper and current lab advisee roster. The older experimental dates are retained explicitly; the new flow study is image generation, not a new robot experiment.
